quest.title: In the Tranquility of Cycles
quest.description: The cabin on the ice seems but a hair's breadth from sinking into the sea. What happened while you were gone? Is the owner of the house, who refused to get ashore, still in there? Approach the cabin to check it out.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

talks.objective: Approach the wooden cabin on the ice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Do you hear that, {NICKNAME}? That rustling, it sounds like it's coming from inside that wooden house...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chulkaturin! Hello! Chulkaturin? Are you still in there?

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Ah, it is you, shorebound travelers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you were inside! Come on out, quickly! The ice is about to melt — your home's gonna sink!

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Yes. The ice is melting away.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Ashore... Thank you, travelers by the shore, but...

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: No, I shall not leave this house.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you serious!? This is not the time for that! If you don't get ashore, you're gonna go under!

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: If this place that I could set my feet upon, this final place that belongs to me, must end in this moment and inexorably sink, then I accept it. This, too, shall be my fate.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: It was I who insisted upon increasing its weight. I wished, in my infinitesimal greed, to restore but a shade of our former glory and dignity, to expand my dwelling, and so overburdened that piece of floe...

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: But this house... No matter the outcome, it is my final resting place. It has borne my flesh, and it carries all my history.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: It and I were ever only relics of the olden times. And if I were to step forth from its doors, I would never again find rooting in this world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about!? Do you mean you're just gonna die?

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: I was always a ghost of history, shorebound travelers. I bear a past I cannot cast aside, indeed, I have borne it long enough.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Anyone can dock by the shore, save for me, traveler, for they have new lives they may live.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: But not me. Should I wish to start a new life, I shall have to atone for the past — the all-too-heavy, all-too-stubborn past, which has long become a part of my life, one I cannot cut free.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: If silence comes in this moment, then I say, let it come. This is the fate I have awaited all these years.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You still have a chance to choose your destiny...

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: And this is my "choice," traveler.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: As long as you know the law the wind follows, even on the river current, you can, in large part, know the path you shall take.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: But on land... Though the wind that sweeps through it has never changed paths in these hundreds of years, this land's future can never be predicted.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Should I step on land... should I tread upon soil estranged and step into its unknowable future, how many of my choices would belong to "me" then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, more and more of the ice is melting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, Chulkaturin, enough of this talk about choices. Come down! We can talk about this stuff later.

choices.text: You can return to the water in the future...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! If you don't wanna live life on land, you can get ashore, build a house just like before, and then it's back to living on water!

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: It can never be just like before, travelers by the shore.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: A new house, even if we do not build it on Snezhnayan land, shall not become a place for me to lay my head.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Were I to build a new house, the wood I would use would never again be the snow poplars I once grew up alongside.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: And the ice, made solid again for this house, would not again bear up the weight of the past.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Were I to lose my past, I would be little different from a rootless piece of floe in the water. Even if we should return to the water, we would shatter and melt at any moment.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: This home is the final anchorage of an elder age, so please, let this elder spirit continue to dwell alongside it.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Thank you, shorebound travelers, my... my friends. Your help once allowed this house, fated to sink, to last for some days more.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Now, I would ask one final thing of you.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Please leave me here. Shatter the brash ice upon the water's surface no longer, pull the house no more, and persuade me not again.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: And if you are willing, please say a last goodbye to me here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chulkaturin...

response.speaker: Sinking house
response.text: (The house makes no reply. It only sinks quietly.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
No familiar sounds come from the house again. For a long while, you hear only a strange song, hummed by someone in an ancient, complex tongue.
Perhaps it tells of the snow poplars yet unfelled, of glories untarnished, of yesterdays yet unsubmerged.
The song grows ever softer, like ever smaller ice blocks melting, melting, turning at last into bubbling foam on the water's surface.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: \nThe ice melts away.

response.speaker: Churkaturin
response.text: Farewell.

choices.text: You can build another home on the ice...
